per_option_rationale.rationale: Student uses log10(2) + log10(3) = 0.3010 + 0.4771 = 0.7781, computing log10(6) instead of log10(12).
Student uses 2 × log10(2) × log10(3) = 2 × 0.3010 × 0.4771, multiplying logs instead of adding them.
Student uses 2 × log10(2) = 0.6020 alone, omitting the log10(3) term.

explanation_sections.approach: Logarithm evaluation problems require factoring the target number into primes whose logs are given. Write the prime factorisation first: 12 = 2² × 3. Then apply log(ab) = log(a) + log(b) and log(a^n) = n × log(a). Substitute the given values last.
explanation_sections.lesson: Always factorise before expanding. Log of a product equals sum of logs. Log of a power equals the exponent times the log.
explanation_sections.timing: About 90 seconds. Factorising 12 takes under 10 seconds. Eliminate option 0.7781 in five seconds: that is log10(6), not log10(12).
